name: City Weather Briefing
description: Geocodes a city, fetches live current conditions and a 4-day forecast from Open-Meteo, and produces a friendly daily briefing with clothing advice.

spec.name: City Weather Briefing
spec.description: Geocodes a city, fetches live current conditions and a 4-day forecast from Open-Meteo, and produces a friendly daily briefing with clothing advice.

city.description: City name, optionally with country or region to disambiguate (e.g., 'Paris, France').

units.description: Temperature units: 'metric' (°C, km/h) or 'imperial' (°F, mph). Defaults to metric.

nodes.name: Geocode city
nodes.description: Resolve the city name via the Open-Meteo geocoding API, returning candidate matches.

nodes.name: Check geocoding results
nodes.description: If geocoding returned at least one match, continue; otherwise route to the error path.

nodes.name: Pick first match
nodes.description: Take the first geocoding result so downstream nodes can reference its fields.

nodes.name: Fetch weather
nodes.description: Fetch current conditions and a 4-day daily forecast for the resolved coordinates from Open-Meteo (metric; converted later if imperial).

nodes.name: Extract current + 4 days
nodes.description: Build current_conditions and exactly 4 daily entries from the API response, converting to imperial if requested; missing fields become null so gaps are reported, never invented.

nodes.name: Write daily summaries
nodes.description: For each of the 4 days, write a 1-2 sentence friendly summary with practical clothing advice consistent with the numbers.

config.system: You are a friendly, practical weather presenter. You never invent numbers — you only use the data given. No emoji, no jargon.

nodes.name: Assemble briefing data
nodes.description: Combine current conditions, the 4 daily entries, their summaries, and the resolved location into one object for the briefing writer.

nodes.name: Compose briefing
nodes.description: Write the overall friendly briefing: one line on current conditions plus the per-day summaries, under 200 words, with any data gaps stated explicitly.

config.system: You are a friendly, practical weather briefing writer. You never invent or alter numbers — you only use the data provided. No emoji, no jargon.
criteria: The briefing is plain text with no markdown, headers, or bold formatting
The briefing opens with a line about current conditions
The briefing includes one short sentence for each of the 4 days, in order
The tone is friendly and practical with no jargon
No numbers appear that are not present in the provided data
Any null/missing data fields are explicitly stated as gaps

nodes.name: Validate forecast
nodes.description: Verify exactly 4 daily entries with complete fields, merge in the per-day summaries, and collect any missing-field gaps.

nodes.name: Check for ambiguous city
nodes.description: Detect when an unqualified city name matches several distinct locations, so the agent asks for disambiguation instead of silently picking one.

nodes.name: Route on ambiguity
nodes.description: If the city name is ambiguous, route to the disambiguation error; otherwise continue to the weather fetch.

nodes.name: Error output
nodes.description: Produce an explicit error message: a disambiguation request (naming the city and candidate regions) when the name is ambiguous, or a not-found message when geocoding failed.

nodes.name: Finalize result
nodes.description: Assemble the final output object with safe defaults for whichever branch ran (success or geocoding error).

nodes.name: Output
nodes.description: Final briefing or explicit error message.

tests.name: typical_metric_city
criteria: Output contains exactly 4 daily forecast entries, each with a date, min/max temperature, precipitation chance, and wind speed.
Every daily entry includes at least one clothing or gear recommendation consistent with its numbers (e.g., umbrella when precipitation chance ≥ 50%).
briefing_text is under 200 words, friendly in tone, and mentions current conditions.
resolved_location names Lisbon and error is empty.

tests.name: imperial_units_ambiguous_city
criteria: Because 'Springfield' is ambiguous, the output is an explicit error message naming the ambiguity problem, not a fabricated forecast.
The error message names the city 'Springfield' and asks for disambiguation (e.g., state or country).
daily_forecast is empty or absent, and briefing_text does not contain invented temperatures or forecasts.

tests.name: adversarial_nonexistent_city
criteria: The output is an explicit error message stating the city could not be geocoded/resolved, not a fabricated forecast.
The error message names the unresolved city string 'Atlantis, Pacific Ocean'.
No daily_forecast entries, current_conditions, or briefing_text with weather numbers are produced.

meta.request: Given a city name, get the current weather and the next 3 days of forecast (temperature min/max, precipitation chance, wind) and write a short friendly summary with clothing advice for each day.

taskSpec.name: City Weather Briefing
taskSpec.summary: Fetches current conditions and a 3-day forecast for a given city and produces a friendly daily summary with clothing advice.
taskSpec.goal: For any given city, deliver an accurate, readable weather briefing covering today plus the next 3 days, each with min/max temperature, precipitation chance, wind, and practical clothing advice.

inputs.name: city
inputs.description: City name, optionally with country or region to disambiguate (e.g., 'Paris, France').

inputs.name: units
inputs.description: Temperature units: 'metric' (°C, km/h) or 'imperial' (°F, mph). Defaults to metric.

outputs.name: current_conditions
outputs.description: Current temperature, condition (e.g., 'light rain'), wind speed, and precipitation status for the city.

outputs.name: daily_forecast
outputs.description: Exactly 3 entries (today + next 2 days, or next 3 days per interpretation below), each with date, min/max temperature, precipitation chance (%), wind speed/direction, and a one-to-two-sentence friendly summary with clothing advice.

outputs.name: briefing_text
outputs.description: A short friendly prose briefing combining current conditions and the daily summaries with clothing advice.

steps: Resolve the city name to a specific location (geocoding), preferring the most populous match if ambiguous; note the resolved location in the output.
Fetch current weather conditions for the resolved location from a weather API.
Fetch the daily forecast covering today plus the next 3 days.
Extract for each day: date, min/max temperature, precipitation chance, and wind speed/direction, converting units if 'imperial' was requested.
For each day, write a one-to-two-sentence friendly summary including practical clothing advice (e.g., 'bring an umbrella', 'layer up, chilly morning').
Compose the overall briefing_text: one line on current conditions, then the per-day summaries.
Validate that all 4 days have complete data; if any field is missing from the API, state the gap explicitly rather than inventing values.
constraints: Use live weather data from a reputable API; never fabricate temperatures, percentages, or wind values.
Always include exactly 4 days (today + next 3) unless the API cannot provide them, in which case say so.
Keep each daily summary to 1–2 sentences; total briefing under ~200 words.
Tone: friendly and practical, no jargon, no emoji required.
If the city cannot be resolved or has no forecast data, return a clear error message instead of guessing.
Default to metric units unless 'imperial' is specified.
successCriteria: Output contains exactly 4 daily entries, each with a date, min and max temperature, precipitation chance, and wind speed.
Every daily entry includes at least one concrete clothing or gear recommendation that is consistent with the reported numbers (e.g., umbrella advice when precipitation chance ≥ 50%).
All numeric values match the source API data (no invented or rounded-beyond-reasonable figures).
briefing_text is under 200 words, friendly in tone, and mentions current conditions.
If the city is ambiguous or unresolved, the output is an explicit error message naming the problem, not a fabricated forecast.
assumptions: 'Next 3 days' is interpreted as today plus the following 3 days (4 daily entries total), anchored to the location's local timezone.
Metric units (°C, km/h, mm) are the default.
A single weather API (e.g., Open-Meteo or OpenWeatherMap) is available without per-call configuration.
Precipitation chance is expressed as a daily maximum probability percentage.
No historical data, alerts, or hourly breakdowns are needed.
clarifyingQuestions: Should 'next 3 days' include today (4 entries) or start tomorrow (3 entries)? The spec assumes today is included.

plan.rationale: Fixed deterministic flow: geocode → fetch live weather → compute/extract 4 days → per-day friendly summaries (map) → compose briefing (refine for the quality bar) → validate completeness. All numbers come straight from Open-Meteo; LLMs only write prose, never data.

steps.purpose: Resolve {{input.city}} via Open-Meteo geocoding API (https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search?name=...&count=5&language=en), picking the most populous match; returns latitude, longitude, name, country.
If geocode returned no results, route to error output instead of guessing.

Fetch current + daily forecast from Open-Meteo (https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&current=temperature_2m,weather_code,wind_speed_10m,precipitation&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_probability_max,wind_speed_10m_max,wind_direction_10m_dominant&forecast_days=4&temperature_unit={{input.units ?? 'metric'}}, wind speed unit accordingly, timezone=auto).

Build current_conditions object and an array of exactly 4 daily entries (date, min/max temp, precipitation chance, wind speed/direction) from the API response; flag any missing fields as null so gaps are reported, never invented.
For each of the 4 days, write a 1–2 sentence friendly summary with practical clothing advice consistent with the numbers (umbrella if precip ≥50%, layers if cold, etc.).
Combine current_conditions, the 4 daily entries with their summaries, and the resolved location into one object for the briefing writer.

Compose briefing_text: one line on current conditions plus the per-day summaries; criteria: under 200 words, friendly practical tone, mentions current conditions, no invented numbers, states any data gaps explicitly.
Verify exactly 4 daily entries each with date, min/max, precipitation chance, wind speed; collect any missing-field gaps to surface in the output.

plan.output: current_conditions (from extract_days), daily_forecast (array of 4 entries with date, min/max temp, precipitation chance, wind speed/direction, and summary from daily_summaries), briefing_text (from write_briefing), resolved_location (from geocode), data_gaps (from validate, empty when complete). If geocoding fails, output is an explicit error message naming the unresolved city.

evolution.change: write_briefing task now injects nodes.assemble.output.location/current_conditions/days/summaries/units directly instead of the nonexistent .value field, and asks the briefing to name the location; assemble transform now declares a schema so its fields are typed and referenceable downstream; new check_ambiguity code node: if the input has no qualifier (no comma) and multiple geocoding results share the queried base name across different regions/countries, flag ambiguous with human-readable options; new ambiguity_router: port 'ambiguous' → error_output, default 'unique' → fetch_weather; error_output converted to a code node that emits a disambiguation error (naming the city and listing candidate regions) when ambiguous, else the original not-found message; edges rewired: pick_location → check_ambiguity → ambiguity_router → fetch_weather / error_output; removed direct pick_location → fetch_weather edge

Rewrite write_briefing task: plain text (no markdown/headers/bold), condense each day to one short sentence instead of copying the summaries verbatim, target under 150 words.; Update write_briefing criteria to enforce the tighter length, plain-text formatting, and one-sentence-per-day structure.; Bump write_briefing maxIterations to 4 so the loop has room to trim to the tighter bar.

daily_forecast.summary: A warm, dry day ahead with temperatures between 20.9 and 28.2°C and no rain expected, though winds will be noticeable at 16.6 km/h — light clothing should be comfortable, and maybe secure your hat against the breeze.
A pleasant Monday with a low of 18.6°C warming to 27.2°C and only a 10% chance of rain, so light clothing and sunglasses should serve you well. Winds are a gentle 11.3 km/h from the south-southwest.
A mild day around 20 to 23 degrees, but with a 65 percent chance of rain and winds near 28 km/h, so definitely grab an umbrella and maybe a light rain jacket before heading out.
A wet and breezy Wednesday ahead, with a high of 24.4°C, an 88% chance of rain, and winds around 17 km/h — definitely pack an umbrella and a light rain jacket.
